Generate a U-shaped profile by subtracting an offset rectangular box from a larger one, ensuring both ends remain open. The larger box should measure 450 mm in length, 70 mm in width, and 40 mm in height. Subtract an inner box that is 60 mm wide and 35 mm and high with same 450mm length, maintain a wall thickness of 5 mm around the sides and base, resulting in a U-shape, open at the top and sides | First, describe in words and step by step how the user's request can be implemented using function calls only. After the description, I will ask you to prepare the function call for execution, but don't execute it until I explicitly request it.

Step-by-step plan – all actions can be achieved with two successive calls to the block-function only.

1. Create the outer, full solid:
   • Use block() with  
     – x_size = [450], y_size = [70], z_size = [40]  
     – x = [0], y = [0], z = [0] (base corner at the global origin)  
     – subtraction = [False] (this establishes the initial volume).

2. Excavate the inner volume to obtain the U-profile:
   • Use a second block() whose dimensions equal the desired hollow space:  
     – x_size = [450]  (the channel runs the entire length, keeping both ends open)  
     – y_size = [60]   (70 – 2·5 ⇒ 5 mm side-wall thickness on each side)  
     – z_size = [35]   (40 – 5 ⇒ 5 mm base thickness)  
   • Offset this void 5 mm from every solid face that must remain:  
     – x = [0]  (no offset; we want the ends open)  
     – y = [5]  (side-wall clearance)  
     – z = [5]  (base clearance)  
   • subtraction = [True]  (it removes material, leaving the U-shape).

No other functions are required; a final finished() call will wrap things up after these two block calls.

Whenever you want the code prepared, just say so and I’ll format the exact JSON payloads for the two block() calls (plus finished()).
